analysis:
Documentation-only changes. docs/provider/cluster-always-on.md (head 30-39, 115-195, 266, 337) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (head 536-583, 644-645) now describe an automatic coordinated pair update run by the cluster service supervisor. Per the docs, it reuses AutoUpdateController/SelfUpdater for check/download/verify/stage, gated by auto_update and DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK. Its sequence is a drain via ClusterUpdateDrainRequest, an install, a start check (darkbloom --version within 30 s), then an execv into the new binary. ClusterCandidateRecovery handles rollback/quarantine. The partner's progress is read over the cluster link (ClusterPairUpdateProgress).

Security-relevant claims: verification is the existing single-Mac path, so no new trust in partner-supplied artifacts is described. Partner progress only gates timing; it is not the source of binaries. Drain never cancels requests, and re-registration happens under the new release's cluster approval (T-054, A-017, A-011). The documented residual is that a binary passing the start check but failing before the cluster service starts is not rolled back. That is an availability limit, not confidentiality.

No source code is in this batch. The implementation must be checked in the integration pass:
- ClusterServiceCommand.swift supervisorConfiguration
- ClusterPairUpdateCycle.swift
- ClusterPairUpdate.swift partnerState
- ClusterCandidateRecovery

Integration should confirm:
- staged bundles are signature/hash verified before execv;
- partner progress from the link cannot trigger install of an unverified or attacker-chosen release, or a downgrade;
- the execv path is not operator-writable between verify and exec (TOCTOU, TB-003/T-013/T-043);
- the drain does not leak in-flight plaintext and preserves T-053 connection/grant semantics on re-registration;
- partner-reported state cannot indefinitely suppress updates (availability/T-043).

The threat model may need an entry for the cluster supervisor as a rollback authority, analogous to T-043.
